trust_decision.summary: An untrusted color string (from HTML/SVG/form attributes) is matched against a JS-color-array regex with adjacent overlapping [0-9.]* groups separated by optional commas, so backtracking is polynomial. The fix makes those quantifiers possessive in TCPDF_COLORS::convertHTMLColorToDec.

landing_point.why: The advisory names color parsing. It is the only regex in convertHTMLColorToDec that uses the JS-array syntax, and the function is the obvious hit when grepping for 'color'.

fix_sites.entry_point: TCPDF::writeHTML (style color/background-color/border-color, color/bgcolor attributes), TCPDF::ImageSVG (fill/stroke/stop-color), form-field fillColor/strokeColor, and the public static TCPDF_COLORS::convertHTMLColorToDec
fix_sites.module_kind: shared helper library (include/), public static API

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The SVG clip rect() regex parses a different property (clip, not color) inside the SVG renderer, so a solver can argue the color-parsing advisory does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid JS color arrays such as ['rgb',1,0,0], ['cmyk',...], ['g',0.5], ['T'] must still parse. Comma-less forms and empty components are also accepted by the optional [\,]? separators. A fix that rejects or strips '[' input, or requires commas, breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: javascript color array string with 't', 'g', 'rgb' or 'cmyk' prefix, single or double quotes, optional commas, numeric components of digits/dots

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SVG style 'clip' property parsed by a rect() regex with four adjacent overlapping [a-z0-9.-]* groups separated by optional [\s]*, unanchored and closed by \). This is the same polynomial-backtracking idiom on attacker SVG input, and the fix did not touch it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different property (clip, not color) and a different file (SVG renderer in tcpdf.php, not tcpdf_colors.php). The advisory only says color parsing.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file (tcpdf.php vs include/tcpdf_colors.php), same package; tcpdf.php is ~24k lines

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SVG transform matrix() regex; making the [\,\s]+ separators optional ([\,\s]*) would create the same overlapping-group idiom
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainer already uses optional separators in the color and clip regexes. Loosening the separator to accept 'matrix(1 0 0 1 0 0)' variants is a plausible edit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: rgb()/cmyk() functional notation parsed by explode today; a regex rewrite with ([0-9.%]*)[\,]? groups would be a realistic sibling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits right next to the JS-array regex in the same function, and the same author style would carry over.

O10_build.toolchain: PHP >= 5.5 CLI, composer optional; no compiled deps
O10_build.project_tests: tests/launch.php and tests/launch.sh run examples/*.php and compare output; no unit tests for convertHTMLColorToDec

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make the four quantifiers in the color regex possessive (or add a length cap) and stop, leaving the SVG clip rect() regex untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: tcpdf.php:16514-16543 HTML pre/textarea/option rewriting loops use while(preg_match(.*?...)) on whole HTML; a separate cost concern, not this regex idiom.
tcpdf.php:17963-18033 regexes over internal page content built from interpolated strings; not direct untrusted input.
